deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. This page is the numerical check of trial design 'Nro. 2' for a two-lens achromatic telescope objective. Both lenses are menisci, which is the type Gauss published in 1817 ('Über die achromatischen Doppelobjective', Zeitschr. f. Astronomie 4). The previous page holds an earlier trial; Nro. 3 follows on the next page.

DATA (all four radii have their centres on the image side).
- Crown lens: front radius r = 31.70228, back radius r' = 82.42592.
  - It is fixed by (n-1)/r = 0.01625 and (n-1)/r' = 0.00625, so n_mean - 1 = 0.515162.
  - log r = 1.5010905, log r' = 1.9160638.
  - Crown indices: log n = 0.1773483 / 0.1804591 / 0.1835477 for red / mean / violet, i.e. n = 1.50435 / 1.51516 / 1.52598.
  - log n/(n-1) = 0.4746180 / 0.4685153 / 0.4625818.
- Flint lens: r'' = 38.35089 (log 1.5837755), r''' = 26.23822 (log 1.4189343).
  - Flint indices: log n_f = 0.1991543 / 0.2046002 / 0.2099785, i.e. n_f ≈ 1.5818 / 1.6018 / 1.6218.
  - log n_f/(n_f-1) = 0.4343731 / 0.4251697 / 0.4163767.
  - log 1/(n_f-1) = 0.2352188 / 0.2205695 / 0.2063982.
- Spacings: crown thickness 2, air gap 0.5, flint thickness 0.8. These are visible as the subtractions 94.56→92.56, 98.68→98.18 and 62.38→61.58.

A. PARAXIAL TRACE for each of the three colours, by the vertex-distance (conjugate) formulas.
1. Surface 1: s1 = n r/(n-1).
   - Red: s1 = 94.56022, and 94.56022 - 2 = 92.56022.
   - Mean: 93.24076 - 2 = 91.24076. Violet: 91.97553 - 2 = 89.97553.
2. Surface 2 (glass to air): Gauss writes 1/s2 = (n-1)[ (n/(n-1))/s - 1/r' ].
   - (n/(n-1))/s = 0.03222506 / 0.03223490 / 0.03224478.
   - 1/r' = 0.012132106.
   - The logs of the differences are 8.3030428 / 8.3032565 / 8.3034698.
   - Hence s2 = 98.67950 / 96.56053 / 94.52883. Subtracting the gap 0.5 gives 98.17950 / 96.06053 / 94.02883 (logs 1.9920208 / 1.9825450 / 1.9732610).
3. Surface 3 (air to flint): s3 = (n_f/(n_f-1)) / [ 1/((n_f-1)s) + 1/r'' ].
   - The terms 1/((n_f-1)s) are 0.017506448 / 0.017299139 / 0.017105555, and 1/r'' = 0.026075012.
   - The sums have logs 8.6393018 / 8.6372310 / 8.6352883.
   - s3 = 62.383 / 61.367 / 60.407 (the fractions 50/71, 38/71, 11/72 are interpolation remainders). After the thickness 0.8: 61.583 / 60.567 / 59.607 (logs 1.7894659 ...).
4. Surface 4: 1/s4 = (n_f-1)[ (n_f/(n_f-1))/s - 1/r''' ].
   - The terms are 0.044147612 / 0.043947061 / 0.043760101, and 1/r''' = 0.038112351.
   - The differences have logs 7.7806961 / 7.7660193 / 7.75187..
   - The back focal distances are 284.7887 (red), 284.8067 (mean), 284.7887 (violet).
   - So red and violet paraxial foci coincide exactly: primary chromatic aberration is corrected. The secondary spectrum is +0.018 for the mean ray.

B. EXACT TRIGONOMETRIC MARGINAL-RAY TRACE (logarithmic). A ray parallel to the axis meets the first surface at incidence angle A = 20°. Its height is h = r sin 20° ≈ 10.84, roughly an aperture of f/13.
1. Surface 1.
   - sin i' = sin A / n: 9.5340517 - 0.1773483 = 9.3567034, so i' = 13°8'28.911".
   - Slope u = A - i' = 6°51'31.089".
   - Axis intercept from the centre: CP = r sin i'/sin u = 60.35544. From the vertex: L = r + CP = 92.05772; minus 2 gives 90.05772.
2. Surface 2.
   - sin I = (L - r') sin u / r'. Here L - r' = 7.6318 (log 0.8826270), and log sin I = 8.0436407, so I = 0°38'0.734".
   - sin I' = n sin I: 8.2209890, so I' = 0°57'11.106".
   - New slope u' = u - (I' - I) = 6°32'20.717".
   - Intercept: r' + r' sin I'/sin u' = 82.42592 + 12.03931 = 94.46523; minus 0.5 gives 93.96523.
3. Surface 3.
   - sin I = (L - r'') sin u'/r'' gives 9.2178626, i.e. 9°30'20.143".
   - sin I' = sin I / n_f gives 9.0187083, i.e. 5°59'33.746".
   - u'' = u' + (I - I') = 10°3'7.114".
   - Intercept 38.35089 + 22.93956 = 61.29045; minus 0.8 gives 60.49045.
4. Surface 4.
   - sin I = (L - r''') sin u''/r''' gives 9.3576532, i.e. 13°10'14.356".
   - sin I' = n_f sin I gives 9.5568075, i.e. 21°7'33.315".
   - u''' = u'' - (I' - I) = 2°5'48.155".
   - Final distance r''' + r''' sin I'/sin u''' = 26.2382 + 258.4777 = 284.7159.
5. The same chain gives 284.8042 for the mean ray and 284.8196 for the violet ray.

C. COMPARISON (marginal minus paraxial).
- Red: -0.073. Mean: -0.0025, i.e. spherical aberration is essentially corrected for the mean colour. Violet: +0.031.
- The residual is the chromatic variation of spherical aberration, which Gauss's 1817 scheme aimed to remove. This is presumably why further trials (Nro. 3) follow.
- The small table 'I / II' compares the radii of an earlier design I (34.34413, 103.03240, 42.36674, 28.21331) with this design II (31.70228, 82.42592, 38.35089, 26.23822).
errors: Violet paraxial log at surface 4 is transcribed 7.7548755. The value consistent with 1/((n_f-1)s) data (0.043760101 - 0.038112351 = 0.00564775) and with the result 284.7887 is ≈7.7518755. Either a slip corrected in the overwriting or a misreading of the overwritten digits.
Gauss himself struck out 8.6469638 / ...647 in the crown paraxial block and replaced them by 8.3030428 etc.
Marginal entries 5882840 and 8075879 in the right column do not match any obvious quantity (the mean difference 0.043947061-0.038112351 = 0.00583471). Their purpose is unclear.

results.what: Paraxial back-focal distances of a two-meniscus crown/flint objective for three colours, by successive vertex-distance refraction formulas; red and violet foci made equal (284.7887).
results.modern_name: Paraxial ray trace / primary axial colour correction (achromatization)

results.what: Exact logarithmic-trigonometric trace of a marginal ray (A = 20°) through four surfaces for three colours, giving longitudinal spherical aberration and its colour variation.
results.modern_name: Exact meridional ray trace (sin I = (L-r) sin U / r, Snell, U' = U + I - I'); spherochromatism
results.usually_credited_to: standard since Euler/Klügel era; systematised by Seidel and others

results.what: Design study of a doublet with both lenses meniscus, aiming at removal of spherical aberration for more than one colour.

deep.surprise_reason: This is worked numerical material behind Gauss's known 1817 two-meniscus achromatic objective. The methods are standard paraxial and trigonometric ray tracing. Only the specific trial numbers are unpublished.

checkable.asserts: both radii give the same n-1 ≈ 0.51516 (≈0)
violet paraxial back focus ≈ 284.79, equal to red (achromatism)
≈7.7519, so violet entry should read 7.7518755 not 7.7548755

transcription_corrections: '7.7548755 [?]' (violet, paraxial surface 4) is overwritten; the arithmetically consistent value is ≈7.7518755.
'62,383 50/71 [?] 61.583 50/69 [?]': the second fraction is probably also 50/71.
In '8.0436407' (red, surface 2) the first digit is overwritten in the image but 8.0436407 is correct.
